images.text: I have been a dog lover my whole life. What's not to love? Like humans they can be kindhearted and personable and at times cheeky and disobedient. Above all, though, they are devoted and loyal friends. If I'm being completely honest, I must admit that I am a little bit obsessed with our furry little canine friends. This obsession dates back to a Christmas that I spent at my grandfather's farm when I was eight. My grandfather had a good-natured golden retriever who insisted on licking my face whenever we arrived. This particular year, she had a litter of puppies. Being a dog lover, I begged my grandparents to give me one of them for Christmas. They told me that I was only eight, and suggested that I wait a few more years before asking for a dog.

On Christmas morning, my brother and I raced downstairs to open our presents. My brother went first. His gift was a brand new racing sled. Filled with anticipation, I tore my package open. It was a small red handkerchief. I acknowledged that I was more than a bit underwhelmed with my present, and honestly, I resented my brother getting a new sled. My grandfather noticed my long face, and he asked me if anything was wrong. I confessed to being a little bit jealous of my brother's gift. My grandfather insisted on being patient. “Good things come to those who wait,” he said. “I guarantee that you will not be disappointed.”

I opened another gift. It was a small toy whistle. Again, I failed to hide my disappointment and again my grandfather told me to keep my chin up. “I promise that you won't be disappointed,” he said. As we began opening our final gifts, I heard a small whimpering coming from my box. I ripped it open and looked inside. Staring up at me was an adorable little puppy. “He can wear the handkerchief around his neck,” my grandfather said, smiling. “And when you want him to come, just blow the whistle.”

Performative verbs are verbs which perform the action they describe. You use these verbs in the Simple Present tense.

Examples of these verbs are:
suggest, acknowledge, admit, advise, apologize, beg, confess, congratulate, declare, deny, forbid, guarantee, name, order, permit , predict, promise, refuse, remind, request, thank and warn.

For example:
I suggest you take the train into the city. Parking Is too expensive.
They request that we read the contract very carefully before signing.
Some verbs (apologize, deny, guarantee, promise and suggest) have the same meaning in either the Simple Present to or Present Continuous forms.

For example:
I don't deny taking the bag. / I'm not denying taking the bag.
You often use modals with performative verbs to make them more polite.

For example:
We would advise you not to take the bus at this time.
